title: Staggered rollforward — customer briefing & post-incident playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for customer-facing communications when we plan a staggered rollforward (model variant swap + regional restart) after a partial degradation event. The audience is technical contacts at impacted customers and internal account leads (SE/AM). Keep it concise, action-oriented, and include prescriptive customer steps when appropriate.

High-level summary (for status page / short update):
- What happened (one line): Between 2029-09-30 22:10 UTC and 2029-10-01 02:45 UTC, a model variant rollout produced elevated tail latency in eu-west-1 for customers using hosted inference.
- Impact: ~18% of requests from some tenant cohorts experienced latency >1.5s and intermittent streaming truncation. No data loss reported.
- Current state (short): Staggered rollforward initiated at 2029-10-01 00:30 UTC — traffic routed to fallback variants in unaffected regions; eu-west-1 is on a rolling revert + optimized variant patch. Customers should expect progressive recovery over next 2–6 hours.

Suggested status page blurb (short form):
Title: Partial latency degradation in eu-west-1 — progressive recovery underway
Body: We detected elevated latency for a subset of hosted inference traffic in eu-west-1. We routed impacted traffic to fallback model variants and initiated a controlled rollforward to a patched variant. Recovery is in progress; customers may see occasional timeouts or slower streaming while we complete the roll. No customer data was lost. We’ll provide another update within 2 hours or when full recovery completes. (link to timeline + FAQ)

Customer-facing timeline (detailed; post-incident to include):
- 2029-09-30 22:07 UTC — Automated alert: 95th/99th tail latency rising in eu-west-1.
- 2029-09-30 22:12 UTC — On-call triage: observed increased prefix KV cache churn correlated with new variant kernel selection.
- 2029-09-30 22:30 UTC — Canary rollback attempted; rollback partially successful but residual queues caused misordered streaming chunks for long-context requests.
- 2029-10-01 00:30 UTC — Staggered rollforward initiated: traffic split to fallback variants and healthy regions per routing policy; disabled auto-batching for impacted queues.
- 2029-10-01 01:50 UTC — Patch deployed to runtime (kernel guardrail + cache eviction tuning) to variant v2-patch.
- 2029-10-01 02:10 UTC — Progressive validation: 99th latency trending down; streaming sessions stable for 80% of impacted tenants.
- 2029-10-01 02:45 UTC — Rolling restart of remaining nodes completed; final validation in progress.
- 2029-10-01 03:15 UTC — Majority recovery; follow-up postmortem being prepared.

Customer guidance (immediate actions):
1) If you observe degraded streaming sessions, try re-opening the client stream after 30s — our routing may reassign to fallback variants.
2) For high-throughput tenants who need strict latency guarantees, temporarily pin to Dedicated or a specific model id compatible with your SLAs (contact SE for expedited scope change).
3) If you depend on ordered token stream for transactional flows, consider adding short client-side buffering of 200–500ms until you receive the final chunk; this avoids partial-commit logic failures.

What we’re doing (technical summary for customers):
- Routing: We activated policy-based routing to move traffic away from eu-west-1 variants showing kernel selection regressions; requests are served from healthy regions/variants when consistent with tenant latency/region policy.
- Runtime patch: Deployed a guardrail that avoids switching to the problematic kernel path for long-context attention patterns and increased local KV cache TTL to reduce churn under bursty traffic.
- Autoscaling controls: Temporarily widened autoscale buffers to reduce frantic node churn during the rollback window.
- Ongoing validation: Synthetic replay of representative prompt sets is running against the patched variant to confirm output parity and latency stability.

Customer postmortem skeleton (what we will share in final):
- Executive summary (impact in plain language, customer-facing apology)
- What happened (timeline + technical root cause: kernel selection + cache eviction race)
- Scope and impact (tenants, regions, request classes) + verification that no persisted data was lost
- What we changed (runtime patch details, routing policy adjustments, QA guardrails added)
- Compensatory actions (credits, SLA remediation, or eng time for migration help as applicable)
- Follow-up commitments (additional testing, observability dashboards made visible to customers, new canary gating)

Draft FAQ (to include on incident page):
Q: Is my data safe?
A: Yes — request payloads and KV cache are ephemeral for inference; no persisted customer data was lost. Any stored logs that were in-flight were either processed or truncated and are being reconciled.

Q: How do you decide which fallback variant to send traffic to?
A: Traffic routing uses a hierarchy: same variant fallback (compatible quantization/architecture) in another region -> different variant with verified parity -> last-resort lower-cost variant with explicit consent options for enterprise tenants.

Q: Will replays produce identical outputs?
A: We can’t guarantee bit-for-bit identical generation after variant substitution, but our patched variants are validated against our prompt set and demonstrate >98% semantic parity across eval metrics.

Open questions / internal notes (for collab):
- Confirm exact list of affected customer IDs (ask billing/ops for final list) — current filter is approximate (JIRA-OPS-9876 has partial tenant list).
- Decide compensation threshold (how long must a tenant have been impacted to qualify) — propose >30 minutes of sustained latency above SLA. Need legal + finance signoff.
- SE playbook: create a short email template for enterprise contacts that explains pinning options and how to request accelerated Dedicated capacity.

Checklist for customer-facing postmortem (to ship):
- [ ] Final tenant list and impact percentages per SLA tier
- [ ] Post-incident synthetic validation artifacts (results + seed prompts) attached
- [ ] Patch diff useful for customer review (high-level)
- [ ] Compensation calculation + approval
- [ ] Customer-facing timeline sanitized for public consumption

Suggested messaging cadence:
- T+0 (immediate): Short status page note + customer-specific banner for affected tenants
- T+2h: Technical status update with preliminary timeline and mitigation steps
- T+24–48h: Customer-facing postmortem draft for review by CS/Legal
- T+72h: Final postmortem + compensation and follow-ups

Notes to self / draft language for SEs to send to customers: 
Hi <customer-name>,
We wanted to update you about an event that affected inference latency in eu-west-1. We routed your traffic to a verified fallback and have completed a staged rollforward to a patched variant. Our investigation shows a kernel selection interaction with long-context caching that caused elevated tail latency for some requests — we’ve deployed a guardrail and are running validation. Please let us know if you still see timeouts; if so provide a sample request id and approximate timestamps and we’ll prioritize an evidence-backed replay.

Attachments to prepare with final doc:
- Timeline CSV (for audit)
- Aggregate latency graphs (per-tenant slices)
- Replay results archive + seed prompts
- Patch release notes (short)
